issues.legal_issue: Open, continuous, peaceful, and non-permissive possession that openly repudiates the claimant’s title and is known to the claimant can mature into ownership by prescription after the required period.
material_facts: The defendants and their predecessors had occupied the land on which their house stood since 1875.
The defendants’ predecessor publicly asserted ownership of that land in 1920, and the plaintiffs knew of that assertion.
The defendants remained in open, continuous, and peaceful possession of the house land, and there was no proof that the plaintiffs or their ancestors had permitted that possession.
The plaintiffs did not bring suit until 1961.
The defendants confined their claim in the appeal to the land on which their house stood.
issues.conclusion: The defendants acquired title by prescription to the land on which their house stood; the plaintiffs’ claim to that portion was dismissed, while their claim concerning the remaining land was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 474 and 505 of the Portuguese Civil Code, possession entails holding or enjoying a thing or right, and acts done by licence or permission do not constitute possession for prescription. Articles 528 and 529 provide for prescription of rights in immovable property through possession, with the applicable period depending on the circumstances described in those provisions. The Court found that the possession was open, continuous, peaceful, hostile to the plaintiffs’ title, and not permissive, and that it lasted long enough to prescribe. The earlier remand decision, reported at AIR 1975 SC 1853, confined the final determination to the plea of prescription; no earlier case was relied on for the substantive prescription rule.

predicates.appeal_from_property_ejectment_suit: The case is an appeal arising from a claim seeking possession of property and removal or eviction of occupants.
predicates.defendants_possessed_house_land_openly_c: The occupants and their predecessors openly, continuously, and peacefully possessed the land on which their house stood.
predicates.defendants_publicly_asserted_own_title: The occupants or their predecessors publicly asserted that they owned the land.
predicates.claimants_knew_of_assertion: The claimants knew that the occupants or their predecessors were asserting ownership against them.
predicates.possession_was_not_permissive: The occupants did not possess the land with the claimants’ permission or licence.
predicates.possession_exceeded_prescriptive_period: The occupants’ possession lasted longer than the period required for ownership to arise by prescription.

issues.definition: When occupants in a property-ejectment appeal openly, continuously, peacefully, and without permission possess house land, publicly assert ownership to the claimants’ knowledge, and remain in possession beyond the required period, they acquire title by prescription to that land.

issues.legal_issue: The rule governing possession held in another person’s name does not apply when the occupants never possessed the land in the claimants’ name.
material_facts: The defendants did not accept that they possessed the house land with the plaintiffs’ permission or in the plaintiffs’ name.
The defendants asserted a lease from a third party, whom the plaintiffs denied had any interest in the land.
The Court found no proof that the defendants’ possession was permissive under the plaintiffs or their ancestors.
issues.conclusion: The rule concerning possession in another’s name did not apply, and the defendants were not required to establish an inversion of title under that rule.
issues.legal_principle: Article 510 of the Portuguese Civil Code addresses possession of a thing in another’s name and provides for prescription only after the title of possession has been inverted in the specified manner. The Court held that Article 510 was inapplicable because the defendants had never possessed the land in the plaintiffs’ name; their alternative assertion of a lease from a third party did not make their possession possession in the plaintiffs’ name.

predicates.appeal_from_property_ejectment_suit: The case is an appeal arising from a claim seeking possession of property and removal or eviction of occupants.
predicates.possession_never_occurred_in_claimants_n: The occupants never held the property on behalf of, or as persons acknowledging possession under, the claimants.

issues.definition: In a property-ejectment appeal, when the occupants never possessed the property in the claimants’ name, the rule for possession held in another person’s name does not apply.

issues.legal_issue: A party claiming a perpetual lease fails to establish that lease when the original instrument is not produced and the evidence is insufficient to prove it.
material_facts: The defendants claimed that their ancestors held the land under a perpetual lease.
The original lease was not produced in court; only a certified copy of a translation of the lease was produced.
The Judicial Commissioner found that the defendants had failed to establish the perpetual lease, and the Supreme Court saw no reason to disagree.
issues.conclusion: The defendants failed to establish their plea of a perpetual lease.
issues.legal_principle: The Court sustained the finding that the perpetual lease had not been proved because the original instrument was not produced and the material produced did not provide a basis to reject the lower court’s conclusion. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this evidentiary conclusion.

predicates.appeal_from_property_ejectment_suit: The case is an appeal arising from a claim seeking possession of property and removal or eviction of occupants.

issues.definition: In a property-ejectment appeal, a claimed perpetual lease is not established when the original lease is not produced and the remaining evidence is insufficient.
